Logos / Brand colours / Approved copy / Social assets Download full kit (.zip) Email the team 01 Logo Four approved variants. Pick the one that fits the background you are placing it on, and keep clear space around it equal to the height of the logo mark. Primary logo Default choice for light backgrounds, decks, and articles. PNG SVG Logo on dark For dark layouts, video overlays, and Void Black backgrounds. PNG SVG Logo mark Square icon for avatars, favicons, and tight spaces. PNG SVG Monochrome One-colour version for print, merch, and low-contrast placements. PNG SVG Logo do's and don'ts Do keep the original proportions and colours. Do leave clear space around the logo so nothing crowds it. Don't stretch, rotate, recolour, or add effects to the logo. body: Pixel Forge Jam Menu About Timeline Theme Rules Prizes Sponsors FAQ Legal Blogs ← Back to all posts Updates Pixel Forge Jam #2 [HAUNTED EDITION] After an incredible first jam, we are officially getting ready for our next one. By Rishabh Mittal 27 June 2026 4 min read When we started Pixel Forge Jam, our goal was simple: create a space where developers, artists, designers, and beginners could come together, make games, learn new skills, and share their work with the world. We did not expect our first jam to grow the way it did. Pixel Forge Jam 2026 brought in over 500 participants, 81 submissions, more than 11,000 views, a prize pool worth over $4,000, and a Discord community of more than 350 members. Seeing so many people join, build, submit, rate games, and support each other was honestly amazing. The best part was not just the numbers. It was seeing people finish real games, try new ideas, collaborate with others, and create projects they could be proud of. Some people joined with experience, while others were trying game development for the first time. That is exactly what Pixel Forge Jam is supposed to be about. Announcing Pixel Forge Jam #2 We are excited to announce that Pixel Forge Jam #2 will run from June 27 to July 4, 2026. It will once again be an online game jam where participants will have one week to create a game based on a theme revealed at the start of the event. title: Announcing Pixel Forge Jam #3 | Pixel Forge Jam

body: Pixel Forge Jam Menu Blogs Back to all posts Announcement Announcing Pixel Forge Jam #3 The forge opens again for a seven-day Tricolor Challenge with more than $5,000 in prizes. By Pixel Forge Team13 August 20264 min read Pixel Forge Jam is back. Developers, artists, designers, musicians, and first-time creators are invited to spend one focused week turning an idea into a playable game. Pixel Forge Jam #3 runs online from September 5 to September 12, 2026. Participants can work solo or in teams of up to four and submit their games through itch.io. The Tricolor Challenge This edition adds one bold creative restriction: every submitted game must visibly use exactly three colours. Engine defaults count, and fades or gradients that introduce extra visible colours are not allowed. The game theme will be revealed when the jam begins. Your entry must respond to that theme, but how you interpret it is up to you. Jam Details DatesSeptember 5-12, 2026 FormatOnline, hosted on itch.io Team sizeSolo or up to four people ChallengeUse exactly three colours ThemeRevealed at the start Prize poolMore than $5,000 in prizes What You Need to Know Use any game engine you like. Create the majority of your work during the jam period and credit any permitted pre-made assets. Generative AI content is not allowed. Include a short explanation of how your game uses the theme. Our first jam completely exceeded our expectations. We had over 500 participants, 81 submissions, more than 900 ratings, and over $4000 in prizes. More importantly, we got to see so many people create, experiment, collaborate, and finish games they can be proud of. Thank you so much to everyone who participated, submitted a game, rated entries, gave feedback, joined the Discord, or supported the jam in any way. body: Pixel Forge Jam Menu Blogs Back to all posts Workshop A Career in Video Games A free two-hour workshop from Karma Play and Pixel Forge for anyone curious about finding their place in the games industry. By Pixel Forge Team23 September 20264 min read Making games is a creative practice, but building a career in games can feel much less clear. This free workshop is designed to make that path easier to see. Join Karma Play and Pixel Forge for two focused hours on the people, skills, and decisions behind a career in video games. What the workshop covers We will look at the different roles that bring a game to life, how portfolios communicate what you can do, and practical ways to start building experience before you have your first professional credit. How game development teams work together. What studios look for in early portfolios and applications. How to choose a first project that demonstrates your strengths. Where to find communities, mentors, and opportunities to keep learning. Workshop details FormatFree online workshop LengthTwo hours Hosted byKarma Play x Pixel Forge AudienceAnyone curious about games careers You do not need to have everything figured out before you start making games. Save your place Bring your questions, your current project, or simply your curiosity. The workshop is a chance to meet other aspiring creators and leave with a clearer next step.
